hypothesis: After the concurrent-io lane's Arc<Value> broadcast (PR #2896, merged as 06f07d119), the remaining per-event supervisor cost at N=100 live sessions is the wakeup+recv+match floor of waking EVERY connected client's event arm on every session event (the source record estimated ~5.9us/session/append). A per-session subscriber registry resolves the delivery set at PUBLISH time (send-time attached check, TS handleWorkerFrame parity): session events enqueue only to the attached connections' bounded per-connection queues, so delivery is O(attached) instead of O(connections). SECONDARY HYPOTHESIS (the parity risk the source record named): moving the attached-check from recv time to send time changes which events a racing attach/detach observes.
ts_parity_case: /home/ubuntu/hillclimb/subscriber-registry/ts-parity-case.md — BUILT FIRST, before any edit. Verdict DEFENSIBLE: TS (origin/main cd1f215cffd, daemon-supervisor.ts) evaluates the delivery set at send time, atomically with the socket write (handleWorkerFrame l.5971 -> the fan-out loop l.6353; attach l.5586 -> session_attached l.5608 in one tick; detach l.5942; no-activeSessionId events DROPPED l.6296-6305, not broadcast). Rust's recv-time check was a TS-impossible superset in the race window (an event published before an attach could still land after it, duplicating a custom row the attach snapshot already carries - pa-tui pushes CustomRow unconditionally on message_start). The registry moves Rust's predicate to the exact TS evaluation point: removes a TS-impossible delivery class, adds none. Section 6 answers the brief's two questions directly (Q1: yes, TS can deliver a message for a session the client just left, exactly when the delivery pass beats the detach delete; the registry reproduces that predicate at the same single instant. Q2: observably equivalent at every client-observable point, with disclosed exceptions D1-D7).
wire_oracle: smoke_registry.py, run on BOTH binaries (twice, reproducible): PASS both. Candidate: exactly 6 session_event frames (3 appends x message_start+message_end) to the attached client; ZERO to an unattached connection (registry isolation); ZERO to a late attacher (the send-time convergence - the old recv-time check could deliver a stale frame); ZERO post-detach. Frame byte-shape parity with the base holds after normalizing run-volatile fields (epoch timestamps, cursor generation): the registry does not change a byte on the wire.
approach: supervisor/subscribers.rs (new): SessionSubscribers registry (session id -> connection id -> bounded mpsc queue) + ClientSubscriptions per-connection handle. Publish resolves the attached set under one registry lock and enqueues; a full queue drops with ONE log line per stall cycle (finding-4a visibility); closed queues prune. All AttachedSession publish sites route through Supervisor::publish_session_event: the worker-relay session_event + side_question_event publishes, the session_binding supersede + rebind notices, the terminal aborted-compaction event, AND the zero-copy splice arm's attach push discovered at the fold (#2897 added a second attach-success site on the tip). ClientRouting::AttachedSession REMOVED (fail-closed: a stale publish fails to compile). Broadcast/BroadcastExcept/RosterSubscribers keep the ring untouched. attach/detach/rebind/disconnect keep registry+list consistent (registry insertion = the delivery boundary; the rebind move is atomic under the registry lock). TARGETED_EVENT_QUEUE_CAPACITY=4096 mirrors EVENT_RING_CAPACITY. 6 new unit tests (routing, isolation, detach instant, rebind move, stall-cycle logging, closed-queue pruning). The dormant supervisor/clients.rs split copy carries the same change (upstream has not declared mod clients yet; re-home disclosure at the fold).
stacking_with_2897: The zero-copy relay (#2897, in the tip) and this registry are STACKED mechanisms on the same routing path and compose cleanly: the relay shares payload BYTES on the worker->client RESPONSE path (spliced client id), while the registry gates the send-time attached SET on the worker->client EVENT path (the ring kept waking every connection per event). The fold's one interaction was the splice arm's attach push, converted to the registry (commit 2677fc146).

The registry's absolute win therefore grows in degraded windows (where hosts actually run hot) and shrinks in clean ones. NO CLAIM is made on the -50% magnitude the naive projection suggested.
